label: requires role
type: the sync function's requireRole() check - the subject write operation is rejected unless the authenticated user holds the named role. Generalizes the single-occurrence requiresChannelAccess/requiresUser/requiresAdminApi predicates found in the same batch (kept as watchlist, distinct nuances, not merged in).
note:
Round 13: recurrence 2 -> 3, but the third file is an error, not growth. normalise-ids.py rewrote 38 misuses of this predicate to requiresServerRole - Server and Capella records using 'requiresRole' to mean 'holds a Server RBAC role', which is a different predicate with a different range. What remains is the two sync-gateway/ records that mean the sync function's requireRole() check, which is what this predicate is, plus three assertions in server/8.0/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/transactions.json whose objects are rbac-role-category:* ids - role *categories*, not roles. Those three were deliberately left alone: neither this predicate nor requiresServerRole has a category in its range, and inventing a requiresServerRoleInCategory on the strength of three occurrences in one file would be minting vocabulary to avoid recording an open question. See reconciliation.md round 13, 'Three open questions left open'.

The lesson for the registry is about how this predicate got misused 38 times: it is the most obvious English name for 'requires a role', it was promoted first, and its record's `type` field explains what it means in terms of Sync Gateway's sync function - which an agent extracting a SQL++ page has no reason to read as excluding their case. A predicate whose name is more general than its meaning attracts exactly this. requiresServerRole and requiresCapellaRole both name their product; this one does not.
